title: How were Post-it Notes invented?

sources.name: 3M — How Silver and Fry found a use for a removable adhesive
National Inventors Hall of Fame — Spencer Silver
National Inventors Hall of Fame — How Art Fry co-invented Post-it Notes

practice: Curious about the stories behind familiar things? Try a mixed round of General Knowledge.

sections.html:
Imagine finding the right song in a book, marking it with a scrap of paper, then watching the marker fall out. For Art Fry, who sang in a church choir, this was a familiar annoyance.

In 1974, that slipping bookmark gave the 3M researcher an idea: perhaps an unusual adhesive developed by his colleague Spencer Silver could hold the marker in place. It needed to stay put, then come off when he wanted to move it.
sections.title: The problem was losing the page

sections.html:
Silver had developed the adhesive in 1968, years before Fry found a use for it. According to 3M, Silver had been aiming for a strong bond. What he made instead allowed surfaces to stick together, separate and stick again.

The adhesive contained tiny spheres, known as microspheres. The National Inventors Hall of Fame describes it as sticky to the touch but with a low level of adhesion. That combination made sense for something you wanted to reposition.

Calling it glue that did not work misses the interesting bit. It could stick. The question was what kind of job needed it to let go.
sections.title: The glue already existed

sections.html:
Fry made sample bookmarks using Silver’s adhesive. When he used them to exchange notes with his supervisor, another possibility became clear: a message could stay attached to a page and still be removed.

Turning that idea into a reliable product took years. The team had to solve manufacturing problems, including keeping the adhesive on the paper and making its grip consistent. Post-it Notes reached the US nationwide in 1980.

Both inventors matter to the story: Silver developed the adhesive; Fry helped turn it into the repositionable note.
sections.title: A bookmark became a message

sections.html:
Picture two jobs: fixing a loose chair leg and leaving a reminder on a page. A permanent bond makes sense for one. For the other, being able to remove the message is part of the point.

Try explaining the invention in three steps: a marker that slips → a grip that releases → a note you can move. Which step connects the laboratory discovery to an everyday problem?

Show the answer

The grip that releases. Fry needed enough hold to keep his bookmark in place, while still being able to move it.

For another object that found an unexpected purpose, discover why bubble wrap began as wallpaper.
sections.title: Would stronger glue have been better?

description: A bookmark kept falling out. A glue was not very sticky. Together, those two problems led to Post-it Notes.
